column1: # Batch 36 — china: what shipped and was then taken out, kept as data.

column3: https://www.als.gov.hk/lookup — Hong Kong's Address Lookup Service. It shipped as a DAILY lookup of the fixed word "central" with n=10: the same ten addresses every run, a query its author typed rather than a source. Re-shaped 2026-10-07 into the entity pivot it really is (q={q}&n=200, SuggestedAddress keyed GeoAddress+street+number; 15 addresses for "central", 7 for "88 Queensway"), probe --check-filter then failed it FILTER_IGNORED: the impossible entity zzqx9nonexistent7q returned 140 addresses against 15 for the real one, because the service is a fuzzy geocoder that matches the 9 and the 7 against house numbers and returns its best guesses for any text (scores 23-50). An entity that is not a Hong Kong address — a company, a person — would get a page of unrelated premises attributed to it, which is rule 4d's confident wrong answer. The API has no minimum-score parameter to re-point at, so the row is removed rather than kept in either shape.
